proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\) satisfy the smooth-chart conditions in the proposed statement, let \(\Omega_P=\{s:p_s>0\}\), and write \(p(P')\) for the observed cell vector induced by a full-data law \(P'\).  We first identify exactly which observed restrictions the fifth-date condition contributes.

The inclusion of observed-law images
\[
 \{p(P):P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\}
 \subseteq
 \{p(P):P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\}                    \tag{1}
\]
follows immediately from \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\).  For the reverse inclusion, fix any \(P^0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\).  Retain the joint law of \((D,Z)\), retain the entire observed untreated path when \(D=0\), and retain the entire observed treated path when \(D=1\).  By consistency these are the only potential-path marginals that determine \(O\).

For each type \(j\), let \(L_j\) be the date-\(3\)-to-date-\(4\) transition of the retained untreated path in cohort \(D=0\); on a conditioning row of probability zero, choose any row supported on \(\mathcal G\), taking the exit row to be \((0,0,1)\).  In cohort \(D=1\), set the untreated path equal to the retained treated path through date \(2\), then draw \(X_3(0)\) from \(U_j[X_2(0),:]\) and \(X_4(0)\) from \(L_j[X_3(0),:]\).  In cohort \(D=0\), set the otherwise unobserved treated path equal to the untreated path through date \(2\) and give it arbitrary Markov continuation kernels supported on \(\mathcal G\).  Couple the two continuations conditionally independently given their common date-\(2\) state.  This construction preserves no anticipation pathwise, preserves both factual path laws, and makes each marginal potential path first-order Markov.  The common \(Q_j\), \(U_j\), and newly common \(L_j\) are used in both cohorts, and every continuation from \(e\) uses the absorbing row.  Hence the resulting full-data law \(\widetilde P\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\) and satisfies
\[
 p(\widetilde P)=p(P^0).                                    \tag{2}
\]
Equations (1)--(2) prove equality of the two observed-law images.  Notice also that the construction leaves the treated cohort's untreated path unchanged through date \(3\), so it leaves \(\theta\) unchanged.  Thus the date-\(4\) common untreated kernel, by itself, supplies no observed restriction and no reduction of the observed tangent space.

We next derive the promised finite score matrix.  For \(s=(d,x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)\), consistency, no anticipation, conditioning on the two values of \(Z\), and the type-conditional Markov factorization give
\[
 p_s
 =\omega_d\sum_{j=1}^2\pi_j^d\mu_j^d[x_0]
 H_j^d[x_0,x_1]Q_j[x_1,x_2]R_j^d[x_2,x_3]T_j^d[x_3,x_4],    \tag{3}
\]
with the constraints displayed in \(\texttt{def:efficiency-handle}\).  For \(d=0\), common untreated transitions and consistency give \(R_j^0=U_j\) and \(T_j^0=L_j\).  For \(d=1\), consistency gives \(R_j^1=V_j\), while \(T_j^1\) is an unrestricted treated factual kernel.  In particular, the treated cohort's common counterfactual \(L_j\) does not occur in (3), confirming the constructive argument above.

Let \(\gamma_0\) be the chart point for \(p\), and abbreviate
\[
 A=Df(\gamma_0),\qquad
 W=\operatorname{diag}(p_s:s\in\Omega_P),\qquad
 S=W^{-1}A.                                                  \tag{4}
\]
Relative interiority on the actual support gives \(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in\Omega_P\), so the inverse in (4) exists.  Since every \(f(\gamma)\) is a probability vector,
\[
 \mathbf 1^{\top}A=0,
 \qquad
 p^{\top}S=\mathbf 1^{\top}WS=\mathbf 1^{\top}A=0.          \tag{5}
\]
Thus every column of \(S\) is a mean-zero score.  If \(\gamma(t)\) is a differentiable chart path through \(\gamma_0\), its observed score is
\[
 h=W^{-1}\left.\frac{d}{dt}f\{\gamma(t)\}\right|_{t=0}
   =S\dot\gamma(0).                                        \tag{6}
\]
Conversely, the locally constant-rank smooth-stratum condition makes every tangent direction to the observed-law image a vector in \(\operatorname{col}(A)\).  Dividing coordinatewise by the positive vector \(p\) shows from (6) that
\[
 \mathcal T_P=\operatorname{col}(S).                        \tag{7}
\]
This is an explicit finite characterization: the variables are the free simplex coordinates in \(\gamma\), their equality and support constraints are solved as specified in the handle, and every entry of \(S\) is the derivative of the displayed polynomial (3).

Let \(\mathbf G\) be the \(|\Omega_P|\times9\) matrix with row \(G_p(s)^\top\), and let \(J=J_{\Phi}(p)\).  By \(\texttt{thm:active-frontier-recovery}\), the causal target equals \(\Phi(p)\) on this model.  By \(\texttt{thm:analytic-gradient}\), \(G_p(s)=J(e_s-p)\).  For a chart direction \(b\), equations (4)--(5) therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\{G_p(O)(Sb)(O)\}
 &=\sum_{s\in\Omega_P}J(e_s-p)(Ab)_s\\
 &=J\left\{\sum_s e_s(Ab)_s-p\sum_s(Ab)_s\right\}
 =JAb
 =\left.\frac{d}{dt}\Phi\{f(\gamma_0+tb)\}\right|_{t=0}. \tag{8}
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(G_p\) represents the derivative on the constrained tangent space.

Put \(Z=W^{1/2}S\).  The elementary Moore--Penrose identity
\[
 Z(Z^{\top}Z)^\dagger Z^{\top}
\]
is the Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{col}(Z)\).  Transforming back from the Euclidean norm to the weighted norm \(\|u\|_W^2=u^{\top}Wu\) shows that the coordinatewise \(L_2(P)\) projection of \(\mathbf G\) onto (7) is
\[
 \mathbf\Psi
 =S(S^{\top}WS)^\dagger S^{\top}W\mathbf G.                \tag{9}
\]
This is exactly the finite weighted least-squares solution in \(\texttt{def:efficiency-handle}\).  Its columns lie in \(\mathcal T_P\), while the columns of \(\mathbf G-\mathbf\Psi\) are orthogonal to \(\mathcal T_P\).  Combining that orthogonality with (8) proves that the rows of \(\mathbf\Psi\) define the unique tangent-space element representing each coordinate derivative; hence they define \(\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}\).

The covariance matrices are
\[
 \Sigma(p)=\mathbf G^{\top}W\mathbf G,
 \qquad
 V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\mathbf\Psi^{\top}W\mathbf\Psi.       \tag{10}
\]
If \(\varphi\) is any other mean-zero influence vector representing the same derivative on \(\mathcal T_P\), then each coordinate of \(\varphi-\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}\) is orthogonal to \(\mathcal T_P\), whereas each coordinate of \(\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_P\).  Therefore, for every \(a\in\mathbb R^9\),
\[
 E_P\{(a^{\top}\varphi)^2\}
 =E_P\{(a^{\top}\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P})^2\}
  +E_P\left[\{a^{\top}(\varphi-\psi_{\mathrm{eff},P})\}^2\right]
 \geq a^{\top}V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)a.                        \tag{11}
\]
Thus (10) is the smallest covariance among influence-function representations on this regular stratum; this is the precise efficiency sense asserted here, without an estimator-attainment claim.

Taking \(\varphi=G_p\) in the same orthogonal decomposition yields
\[
 a^{\top}\{\Sigma(p)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}a
 =\|(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})a^{\top}G_p\|_{L_2(P)}^2.        \tag{12}
\]
The right side is positive exactly when \(a^{\top}G_p\notin\mathcal T_P\).  Equations (3)--(4) and (9) make both sides computable from the finite mixture chart.  Equality of observed-law images in (1)--(2) proves that any strict reduction relative to the saturated covariance is caused by the observable mixture, Markov, support, and common pre-treatment \(Q_j\) restrictions in (3), not by the common date-\(4\) untreated counterfactual transition.  The proof establishes neither existence of a regular estimator attaining (10) nor a uniform result across support or Jacobian-rank changes, and the proposed statement makes neither assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under \(\texttt{ass:two-types}\), \(\texttt{ass:cohort-overlap}\), \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:no-anticipation}\), \(\texttt{ass:markov-paths}\), and \(\texttt{ass:common-date-two-transition}\), the matched-slice rank condition \(\texttt{ass:four-slice-rank}\) implies
\[
 \min_{d\in\{0,1\},\,j\in\{1,2\}}\pi_j^d>0.
\]
Thus positive latent-type masses are a consequence of the active-slice rank condition and need not be imposed separately.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(d\in\{0,1\}\).  Cohort overlap makes all probabilities conditional on \(D=d\) well defined.  For \(x,y\in\mathcal A\), define
\[
 B_x^d[u,j]
 :=P(Z=j,X_0=u,X_1=x\mid D=d),
 \qquad
 D_{xy}:=\operatorname{diag}\{Q_1[x,y],Q_2[x,y]\},
\]
and define the \(2\times2\) matrix \(\bar C_y^d\) by
\[
 \bar C_y^d[j,v]
 :=P(X_3=v\mid X_2=y,Z=j,D=d),
 \qquad v\in\mathcal A.
\]
Consistency identifies the observed cohort path with potential path \(d\), and no anticipation identifies its coordinates through date \(2\) with those of the untreated path.  The type-conditional Markov property and the common date-\(2\) transition therefore give, for \(u,v\in\mathcal A\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \bar A_{xy}^d[u,v]
 &=\sum_{j=1}^2
   P(Z=j,X_0=u,X_1=x\mid D=d)\,
   Q_j[x,y]\,
   P(X_3=v\mid X_2=y,Z=j,D=d)\\
 &=\{B_x^dD_{xy}\bar C_y^d\}[u,v].
                                                               \tag{1}
\end{aligned}
\]
Suppose that \(\pi_{j_0}^d=P(Z=j_0\mid D=d)=0\) for one of the two type labels.  Nonnegativity then implies
\[
 B_x^d[u,j_0]
 \leq P(Z=j_0\mid D=d)=0
 \qquad(u,x\in\mathcal A),                                  \tag{2}
\]
so column \(j_0\) of \(B_x^d\) is zero.  Since there are exactly two types, \(\operatorname{rank}(B_x^d)\leq1\).  Equation (1) consequently yields
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(\bar A_{xy}^d)
 \leq \operatorname{rank}(B_x^d)
 \leq1.                                                       \tag{3}
\]
This contradicts \(\texttt{ass:four-slice-rank}\), under which every \(2\times2\) active slice is nonsingular and hence has rank \(2\).  Thus \(\pi_j^d>0\) for both \(j\).  Since \(d\) was arbitrary and there are finitely many \((d,j)\), their minimum is strictly positive.

added_lemmas.statement: The observed-law images of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\) and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\) are equal.  More precisely, for every \(P^0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\) there is a law \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\) inducing the same observed cell vector \(p\) and the same first-post causal target \(\theta\).  Consequently, the common date-\(4\) untreated transition restriction alone supplies neither an observed-law restriction nor an observed tangent-space reduction.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(p(P')\) for the observed cell vector induced by a full-data law \(P'\).  Since \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\),
\[
 \{p(P):P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\}
 \subseteq
 \{p(P):P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\}.                  \tag{1}
\]
For the reverse inclusion, fix \(P^0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}\).  Retain the joint law of \((D,Z)\), retain the entire observed untreated path when \(D=0\), and retain the entire observed treated path when \(D=1\).  By consistency these are the only potential-path marginals that determine \(O\).

For each type \(j\), let \(L_j\) be the date-\(3\)-to-date-\(4\) transition of the retained untreated path in cohort \(D=0\); on a conditioning row of probability zero, choose any row supported on \(\mathcal G\), taking the exit row to be \((0,0,1)\).  In cohort \(D=1\), set the untreated path equal to the retained treated path through date \(2\), then draw \(X_3(0)\) from \(U_j[X_2(0),:]\) and \(X_4(0)\) from \(L_j[X_3(0),:]\).  In cohort \(D=0\), set the otherwise unobserved treated path equal to the untreated path through date \(2\) and give it arbitrary Markov continuation kernels supported on \(\mathcal G\).  Couple the two continuations conditionally independently given their common date-\(2\) state.

This construction preserves no anticipation pathwise, preserves both factual path laws, and makes each marginal potential path first-order Markov.  The common \(Q_j\), \(U_j\), and newly common \(L_j\) are used in both cohorts, and every continuation from \(e\) uses the absorbing row.  It preserves the cohort and type laws and every observed matched slice, so the rank and spectral conditions are unchanged.  Hence the resulting full-data law \(\widetilde P\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\) and satisfies
\[
 p(\widetilde P)=p(P^0).                                    \tag{2}
\]
This proves the reverse inclusion and hence equality of observed-law images.

It remains to verify preservation of the causal target rather than create it by definition.  The construction leaves the joint law of \((Z,X_3(1))\) given \(D=1\) unchanged.  It also leaves the treated cohort's untreated path unchanged through date \(2\) and applies the same common kernel \(U_j\) at date \(3\) as \(P^0\).  Iterated expectation therefore gives, for every \(j\in\{1,2\}\) and \(y\in\mathcal S\),
\[
 \widetilde P\{Z=j,X_3(0)=y\mid D=1\}
 =\sum_{x\in\mathcal S}
   P^0\{Z=j,X_2(0)=x\mid D=1\}U_j[x,y]
 =P^0\{Z=j,X_3(0)=y\mid D=1\}.                            \tag{3}
\]
Thus every type contribution \(\nu_j\), and consequently their aggregate \(\tau\), is unchanged.  By the definition \(\theta=(\nu_1^\top,\nu_2^\top,\tau^\top)^\top\), it follows that \(\theta(\widetilde P)=\theta(P^0)\).  Finally, the only parameters removed by imposing a common date-\(4\) untreated kernel in the treated cohort govern \(X_4(0)\) after treatment and never enter the observed law.  Their observed scores are zero.  Hence the restriction alone cannot reduce the observed tangent space.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\), and suppose its observed law \(p\) is in the relative interior of an actual-support, fixed-latent-support chart from \(\texttt{def:efficiency-handle}\) on which the mixture Jacobian has locally constant rank and its image is a smooth embedded stratum.  If \(A_{\gamma}=Df(\gamma)\), \(W_p=\operatorname{diag}(p_s:p_s>0)\), and \(S_{\gamma}=W_p^{-1}A_{\gamma}\), then \(\mathcal T_P=\operatorname{col}(S_{\gamma})\).  Writing \(\mathbf G_p\) for the matrix with row \(G_p(s)^\top\), the constrained canonical gradient of \(\theta=\Phi(p)\) and its covariance are explicitly
\[
 \mathbf\Psi_P
 =S_{\gamma}(S_{\gamma}^\top W_pS_{\gamma})^\dagger
  S_{\gamma}^\top W_p\mathbf G_p,
 \qquad
 \psi_{\mathrm{eff},P}(s)=\mathbf\Psi_P[s,:]^\top,
 \qquad
 V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\mathbf\Psi_P^\top W_p\mathbf\Psi_P.
\]
This covariance is minimal among influence-function representations of the derivative on \(\mathcal T_P\), and, for every \(a\in\mathbb R^9\),
\[
 a^\top\{\Sigma(p)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\}a
 =\|(I-\Pi_{\mathcal T_P})a^\top G_p\|_{L_2(P)}^2.
\]
Thus strict reduction from the saturated covariance in direction \(a\) occurs exactly when \(a^\top G_p\notin\mathcal T_P\).  The formula is computable by differentiating the finite products and solving the simplex constraints in \(\texttt{def:efficiency-handle}\).  No existence or attainment claim for a regular likelihood or one-step estimator, and no uniform constrained-efficiency claim across support or Jacobian-rank changes, is made.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current claim asserts a computable constrained bound and pointwise likelihood or one-step attainment while defining the score space only as an unspecified closure. The proposed statement narrows to smooth constant-rank mixture charts, exposes the complete finite mixture map, Jacobian, simplex constraints, and weighted projection, and removes the unproved attainment conclusion. A separate proved proposition in the same bundle corrects the claim that the date-4 counterfactual equality shrinks the observed-law image.

proposed_core_edits.reason: With exactly two types, nonsingularity of an active matched slice forces both type columns to be nonzero and hence forces every cohort-specific type mass to be positive; the new rank-implies-overlap lemma supplies this fact, so a separate maintained overlap premise is redundant.

proposed.name: Broad absorbing support model
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{face}}=\{P:P\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:consistency},\text{ass:no-anticipation},\text{ass:two-types},\text{ass:cohort-overlap},\text{ass:markov-paths},\text{ass:absorbing-exit},\text{ass:common-date-two-transition},\text{ass:common-first-post-untreated-transition},\text{ass:four-slice-rank},\text{ and }\text{ass:simple-cycle-spectrum}\}\). Date-\(1\) absorption is allowed, and no date-\(4\) common-kernel restriction is imposed.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Remove the redundant type-overlap premise from the broad model; positivity is now derived from two types, cohort overlap, Markov factorization, and active-slice rank.

proposed.name: Finite Markov-mixture tangent projection handle
proposed.construction:
Fix a law \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{5d}}\), its actual observed support \(\Omega_P=\{s:p_s>0\}\), and fixed latent supports for every simplex row.  A local free-coordinate vector \(\gamma\) consists of the cohort probability \(\omega_1=P(D=1)\), one free type mass \(\pi_1^d\) per cohort, the initial probabilities \(\mu_j^d[x]=P(X_0=x\mid Z=j,D=d)\), and the nonfixed entries of the rows of \(H_j^d,Q_j,R_j^d\), and \(T_j^d\).  Impose
\[
 \omega_0=1-\omega_1,\qquad \pi_2^d=1-\pi_1^d,
 \qquad R_j^0=U_j,qquad R_j^1=V_j,qquad T_j^0=L_j,
\]
while \(T_j^1\) is the unrestricted treated factual date-\(4\) kernel.  Every stochastic vector or nonabsorbing row is represented by its positive free entries, with one supported entry set equal to one minus their sum; structural zeros are held fixed and the absorbing row is \((0,0,1)\).  For \(s=(d,x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)\in\Omega_P\), define the observed mixture chart
\[
 f_s(\gamma)
 =\omega_d\sum_{j=1}^2\pi_j^d\mu_j^d[x_0]
 H_j^d[x_0,x_1]Q_j[x_1,x_2]R_j^d[x_2,x_3]T_j^d[x_3,x_4].
                                                               \tag{1}
\]
At a chart point \(\gamma_0\) with \(f(\gamma_0)=p\), calculate
\[
 A_{\gamma_0}=Df(\gamma_0),\qquad
 W_p=\operatorname{diag}(p_s:s\in\Omega_P),\qquad
 S_{\gamma_0}=W_p^{-1}A_{\gamma_0}.                          \tag{2}
\]
All entries of \(A_{\gamma_0}\) are obtained by differentiating the finite products in (1), and \(\operatorname{col}(S_{\gamma_0})\) is the computed chart score span.  If \(\mathbf G_p\) is the \(|\Omega_P|\times9\) matrix with row \(G_p(s)^\top\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{eff}}\) returns the candidate projected-gradient matrix and covariance
\[
 \mathbf\Psi_P
 =S_{\gamma_0}(S_{\gamma_0}^{\top}W_pS_{\gamma_0})^\dagger
  S_{\gamma_0}^{\top}W_p\mathbf G_p,
 \qquad
 V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\mathbf\Psi_P^{\top}W_p\mathbf\Psi_P. \tag{3}
\]
Equivalently, for each reported coordinate \(\ell\), (3) is the fitted value in the explicit finite optimization
\[
 \min_{b\in\mathbb R^{\dim(\gamma)}}
 \sum_{s\in\Omega_P}p_s\{G_{p,\ell}(s)-S_{\gamma_0}[s,:]b\}^2. \tag{4}
\]
The Moore--Penrose inverse makes the fitted value invariant to redundant chart coordinates.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace the opaque instruction to differentiate unspecified restrictions with an explicit two-type Markov-mixture probability chart, solved simplex and support constraints, its finite Jacobian score matrix, and the exact weighted least-squares optimization.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The date-4 common untreated condition restricts the full counterfactual law but, as proved by the replacement theorem, does not shrink the observed-law image; its role must not advertise a distinct observed efficiency domain.

proposed.justification: The explicit finite mixture Jacobian makes the smooth-stratum tangent projection and its weighted least-squares covariance evaluable.
proposed.gap: The result is local to fixed-support, fixed-latent-support, constant-rank smooth strata and does not prove existence, regularity, or attainment for a likelihood or one-step estimator.
proposed.consumer: Given fitted chart coordinates on a regular stratum, an analyst can differentiate the displayed cell-probability products and solve the finite weighted least-squares problem; otherwise the saturated guarded bands remain the justified procedure.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Synchronize the narrowed claim with the explicit finite chart and remove the opaque attainment and uniformity basis.

prose_updates.tldr:
Four matched active-state slices identify the unnormalized latent-type sublaws among units active at date \(1\), even when a common absorbing state makes all-state terminal factors singular and some units are already absorbed. Spectral projectors fix scale, terminal row sums recover exit probabilities, and a full-row-rank pseudoinverse transports the second active predecessor factor. Absorption plus no anticipation makes initially absorbed units' treatment effects zero, so the type contributions \(
u_j\), at-risk effects \(
u_j/\alpha_j^1\), and aggregate ATT \(	au=\sum_j
u_j\) are point identified over the full broad fiber. The observable no-date-\(1\)-absorption subface additionally identifies full type masses and conditional type effects. The corrected analytic \(126\)-cell map has a saturated multinomial canonical gradient and guarded multiplier bands with uniform coverage under singular correlation. On a separate smooth constant-rank chart, the observed Markov-mixture tangent projection is an explicit Jacobian-weighted least-squares calculation; the date-\(4\) counterfactual equality does not shrink the observed-law image, and no constrained-estimator attainment claim is made.

sampling_model.overlap: Both cohorts have positive probability. With exactly two types, nonsingularity of the active matched slices implies positive active mass for each type and cohort, hence positive full type mass; no separate latent-type overlap premise is imposed.

prose_updates.related_work: Ahn and Kasahara (2026), Proposition 14 and Appendix A.4, provide the closest causal setup and inverse-cancellation architecture, but their stated full-rank and positive-transition hypothesis class excludes the common absorbing boundary; the present result is an excluded-boundary extension, not an application of that class. Higgins and Jochmans (2023) and Gupta, Kumar, and Vassilvitskii (2016) reconstruct Markov mixtures under their respective time-homogeneity, component-rank, state-count, and nondegeneracy regimes; those scaling and label ideas are prior art, while the present theorem is a causal, time-varying active-minor result and does not subsume them. Restricted hidden-Markov measurement results likewise answer reconstruction questions under their own emission or structural restrictions, not the potential-path contribution identity proved here. Deaner and Ku (2026) motivate transition restrictions for absorbing duration outcomes but study aggregate duration difference-in-differences rather than latent-type multi-state reconstruction. Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2017) motivate differentiating diagonalization estimators; Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013, 2015) provide neighboring Gaussian bootstrap and anti-concentration tools. Newey (1990) supplies the general tangent-projection perspective; here the only constrained calculation is the explicitly differentiated finite Markov-mixture chart on a fixed-support constant-rank stratum, without an attainment claim. Rao and Risch (2026) are the interpretation consumer: an incumbent-firm panel could use active productivity states and exit to study offsetting latent-type contributions, but this note does not claim their data satisfy its model or iid sampling assumptions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance \(\Sigma(p)\) is the efficiency bound for the specified off-model continuation \(\Phi\) in the saturated multinomial support-stratum model. On a fixed-support, fixed-latent-support smooth Markov-mixture chart of locally constant Jacobian rank, the projected covariance is computable from the explicit cell-probability Jacobian and is minimal among influence-function representations on that tangent space. The argument does not prove existence or attainment by a likelihood or one-step estimator, and it does not cover support or rank changes uniformly. The common date-\(4\) untreated condition restricts an unobserved treated-cohort counterfactual continuation and therefore does not shrink the observed-law image; it is not itself a source of efficiency gain. The exact multiplier quantile is the mathematical object; a fixed number of Monte Carlo draws needs a separate approximation error analysis. The sharp-frontier pair changes full latent type shares and full conditional type effects while preserving active shares, at-risk effects, both contribution vectors, and the entire aggregate ATT vector.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proposal proves a sufficient constructive frontier for two known latent types, two active states, one absorbing exit, four nonsingular matched active slices, simple common cycle signatures, cohort overlap, type-conditional first-order Markov potential paths, no anticipation, and common untreated date-\(2\) and first-post kernels. Positive type masses are derived from two-type slice rank rather than separately assumed. It does not establish necessity beyond the explicit initial-absorption pair, identify unknown type count, handle weak eigengaps, justify clustered policy-panel inference, or allow approximate common transitions. Full conditional type effects require the observable no-date-\(1\)-absorption subface; the broad class identifies active sublaws, type contributions, at-risk effects, and the aggregate. The date-\(4\) common counterfactual kernel defines a full-data subclass with the same observed-law image; the explicit tangent projection is only a smooth fixed-support, constant-rank characterization and carries no estimator-attainment or uniform-efficiency guarantee.
